fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Paul says the son by the slave woman "…was born according to the flesh…" (Galatians 4:23). That's the first blank. His brother, the son by the free woman, was born through the promise, so Paul sets the two births side by side. Flesh on one side, promise on the other.

Right on, baker. The son by the free woman "…was born through the promise." (Galatians 4:23). That's the second blank. Paul sets that against his brother, who was born according to the flesh, so the two sons are told apart by how they were born.

Prophets is a fair guess, baker, but it isn't in this verse. Paul says one son was born "…according to the flesh…" and the other "…through the promise." (Galatians 4:23). Flesh goes with the son by the slave woman. Promise goes with the son by the free woman.

Carmel isn't the mountain Paul names, baker. He says, "One covenant is from Mount Sinai and bears children into slavery…" (Galatians 4:24). Sinai is where that covenant comes from. That's the name to hold onto.

Sarah isn't the name Paul gives, baker. He names the Sinai covenant, the one that bears children into slavery, and says, "This is Hagar." (Galatians 4:24). Paul sets that woman against the free woman he mentions in Galatians 4:22. Easy to flip them, so don't be hard on yourself.

Rebekah isn't named in this passage, baker. Paul says the covenant from Mount Sinai "…bears children into slavery: This is Hagar." (Galatians 4:24). The two women he's pointing to are the slave woman and the free woman (Galatians 4:22). Hagar is the name he gives to the Sinai covenant.

You got it, baker. The words say, "…more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband." (Galatians 4:27). That's the reason she's told to rejoice. The children of the desolate woman are more than the children of the woman who has a husband.

Ishmael is a natural pick, baker, since he's the son Hagar bore to Abram (Genesis 16:15). But Paul says, "Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise." (Galatians 4:28). His comparison goes to Isaac, the son born through the promise (Galatians 4:23).

Esau is a Bible name, baker, but he isn't in this passage. Paul says, "Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise." (Galatians 4:28). Isaac is the one he compares them to. Esau was Isaac's son (Genesis 25:24–26), so you're in the right family, just one name off.

That's right, baker. Paul closes with, "Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman." (Galatians 4:31). So the believers belong to the free woman, not the slave woman. With that one line, Paul seals the whole cookie box and stamps it.
